title: Model hotstore consistency & eviction architecture review notes
content:
Meeting: Model Hotstore Consistency & Eviction — Architecture Review
Date: 2026-03-01
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Diego Ruiz, Maya Chen, Evan Hollis, Rhea Kapoor (notes), James O'Neill (SRE consult)
Purpose: Review proposed design for a model-level hotstore that holds decoded KV prefixes and short-term model artifacts, decide on consistency/eviction semantics, and produce an actionable migration plan for Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
Context / Background:
- Motivation: Hotstore is intended to reduce token-level compute by keeping frequently-accessed model prefixes and per-conversation KV slices resident in GPU RAM across requests. Current prefix caching lives in the request runtime with brittle eviction causing repeated cold starts for long-running conversations.
- Constraints: Must support multi-variant routing (canary fallbacks), private deployments with restricted networking (no cross-VPC coordination), and bounded memory per GPU. Any protocol cannot add >5ms median p95 latency overhead for cache lookup in the critical path.
- Existing work: prototype in PR 2148 implements a single-owner in-GPU hotstore keyed by (model-version, shard, conv-id prefix-hash). It uses LRU with per-shard quotas. Observed issues: race on concurrent writes, inconsistencies across replicas during rollouts, and high eviction churn under polyglot workloads.
Discussion summary (options evaluated):
Option 1 — Strong per-shard consistency with centralized lease manager
- Design: A lightweight coordinator (leader per rack) hands out leases for hotstore keys to writers; writers refresh leases and only the lease-holder can mutate entries. Eviction decisions are centralized to avoid duplicate caching.
- Pros: Eliminates write races, deterministic ownership simplifies invalidation during model rollouts.
- Cons: Requires cross-node coordination (problematic for Private deployments), adds ~2–4ms for lease check in critical path unless optimized to local cache. Single point of failure mitigations add complexity.

Option 2 — Best-effort epoched consistency with monotonic stamps
- Design: Writers attach an epoch and monotonic counter to entries; readers pick highest epoch/counter and stale entries naturally superseded. No central coordinator. Rollouts increment epochs. Eviction is local LRU with global hints via non-strong gossip (best-effort).
- Pros: Simple, robust for Private, low latency overhead. Rollouts handled by epoch bump.
- Cons: Potential temporary duplication across GPUs and slightly higher memory use. Harder to ensure deterministic eviction order across replicas.

Option 3 — Hybrid: lease-less writes + periodic reconciliation
- Design: Allow local writes without leases but run background reconciler that de-duplicates and evicts low-value duplicates. Reconciliation jobs run per-model with backoff.
- Pros: Low-latency writes, tolerates Private deployments, eventual convergence.
- Cons: Reconciler adds background load; transient inconsistencies remain.
Decision (consensus):
- Adopt Option 2 (Epoched stamps + local LRU + lightweight global hints) as default for Hosted and Private deployments. Rationale: preserves low-latency critical path, simplifies Private deployment constraints, and minimizes implementation complexity. The team accepts duplicate entries as tradeoff for lower tail latency and simpler operations.
- Add a configuration flag for Dedicated clusters to enable Option 1 (lease-based) under customer request where strict determinism is required and cluster networking allows it.
Tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Memory duplication: mitigate by per-model quotas and adaptive admission (reject hotstore entries if working set > threshold). Add a telemetry gauge for duplicate-entry ratio and hotstore RAM usage per GPU.
- Rollouts and invalidation: rollouts increment model epoch. Edge case: overlapping epoch windows may cause brief mixed-epoch reads. Mitigate by having rollout controller publish a rollout-commit timestamp and samples-only quiesce window for canary traffic.
- Eviction fairness: local LRU can starve long-tail conversations. Add a low-frequency promotion metric: if a conversation's prefix is hit >X times in Y seconds, it gets a reserved mini-quota to prevent repeated evictions.
Operational requirements / metrics:
- New metrics to emit: hotstore_total_entries, hotstore_duplicate_ratio, hotstore_evictions_per_minute, hotstore_insert_latency_p50/p95, hotstore_memory_pressure_by_gpu, hotstore_epoch_mismatch_count.
- SLOs: insert latency p95 < 5ms added; duplicate_ratio < 15% under steady-state for typical chat workloads.
- Alerting thresholds: memory_pressure > 85% -> trigger autoscale or throttle admissions; evictions_per_minute spike 3x baseline -> investigate workload skew.
Migration & rollout plan:
1) Implement epoch stamps in runtime and a server-side rollout-epoch controller (conservative API). Unit tests + model compatibility checks (2 weeks).
2) Canary in Hosted with small percentage of traffic and detailed telemetry (1 week). Observe duplicate_ratio and p95 latency.
3) Ramp to 50% after no regressions; enable adaptive admission. Monitor metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Document Dedicated opt-in lease-mode and provide migration steps for customers.
5) Private deployments: enable epoch mode by default; create a simple configuration knob for memory quotas.
Action items (owners and ETA):
- Aisha: Draft design doc for epoch stamps & admission controller (due 2026-03-08).
- Diego: Implementation spike for stamped write path + tests (due 2026-03-19).
- Maya: Telemetry dashboard mockups and alerts (due 2026-03-12).
- Evan: Cost simulation for duplicate-memory scenarios using representative workload traces (due 2026-03-15).
- James: SRE runbook for hotstore OOM scenarios and emergency eviction policy (due 2026-03-10).
Open questions / follow-ups:
- Rollout quiesce window sizing: what is a safe default for low-latency services? (Action: small benchmark in week of 2026-03-08).
- Admission policy heuristic: should we prefer recency or frequency? Proposal: frequency-first but include recency floor. (Owner: Aisha to propose tunable defaults)
- Dedicated lease-mode API shape: what surface do we expose to customers vs internal-only? (Owner: Diego + Product to sync)
Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on coordination. If product requests strict determinism for enterprise customers we have a clear path (lease mode) that can be toggled.
- Please review the linked PR and Confluence draft for implementation notes and provide comments inline by 2026-03-09.
End of notes.
